question: to the Commission Jorge Buxadé Villalba (PfE) Subject:

When the war between Russia and Ukraine started, the EU made EUR 193.3 billion available to Ukraine, of which EUR 17 billion supposedly went to Member States to support those fleeing the war. The latter figure is three times the amount Spain receives annually under the common agricultural policy. However, although the funds were made available, that did not mean that the abovementioned amount was granted directly; instead, Member States were allowed to reallocate that sum for the purpose in question from sources such as the cohesion policy funds for the 2014-2020 period and REACT-EU funds. In light of the above: 1.
How much of those EU funds has Spain certified that it reallocated between 2022 and 2025 for measures to help Ukrainians displaced by the war?
What amounts have the Member States reallocated from the above EU funds for the purpose in question?
What traceability mechanisms has the Commission applied to monitor the destination of the funds?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (31.7.2026) 1-2. Cohesion policy supports a broad range of migration-related measures. With the approval of a set of Regulations for refugees in Europe1, funding flexibility was increased, for example through additional liquidity (amounting to about EUR 13.7 billion overall, out of which about EUR 1.8 billion for Spain2). This mainly served to take pressure off Member States’ national budgets negatively impacted by the Russian military aggression. In addition, 18 Member States and the UK3 mobilised EUR 1.4 billion4 in cohesion policy programmes, out of which EUR 0.26 billion allocated by Spain to support displaced people from Ukraine by providing accommodation, healthcare, employment orientation, medical, social and psychological support. 3. Measures relevant to migration-related policies were subject to the Commission’s regular monitoring based on programme data reported by Member States, including common output indicators. Additionally, in their final implementation report on 2014-20205, Member States had to explain how some CARE6-related requirements were fulfilled. An ex post evaluation7 which covered expressly the Ukrainian refugee crisis was also conducted.
